source.version_note: Cognitive, Affective, & Behavioral Neuroscience18(5),837–856; online10 July2018, print October2018. Publisher PDF; Crossref and publisher verify identity and both date types.
source.verification_method: All20 supplied pages and full bibliography read. All11 figures and four tables visually inspected on PDF5–14; the public one-page TableS1 was downloaded, fully read and visually checked. Crossref verifies main identity and corrected Cullen/Özdem source metadata. Selected chi-square tail probabilities and trial-count arithmetic checked; no raw behavioral/neuroimaging data, maps or executable models obtained.

citation.title: Seeing minds in others: Mind perception modulates low-level social-cognitive performance and relates to ventromedial prefrontal structures

reading.source_scope_note: N=22 human participants judge six static robot-to-human face morphs during fMRI, then perform a counterpredictive gaze-cueing task outside the scanner. Mind ratings, physical appearance and reaction-time differences are not actual robot mentality or a uniquely identified causal neural mechanism. The planned four-run mind-rating analysis is correction-null; its significant counterpart is a disclosed post hoc two-run analysis.
access_limits: No raw trial records, reaction-time exclusions/error summaries, design matrices, random-effects specification, code, unthresholded statistical maps or full model output obtained. Reported repeated-measures analysis uses mixed models, but exact random-effects/scoring implementation remains unclear.

All eleven figures, four tables and the complete one-page supplementary question list were read. The supplement visibly lists23 questions despite the main text’s24; the missing item and actual trial count cannot be inferred.

Cited original mirror-neuron, motor-interference, joint-attention, social-facilitation, lesion and gaze-cueing sources are not independently fully read merely through this bibliography. Motor resonance is a background construct, not directly tested in this study.

fMRI is collected during mind judgments only. No neural recording during the later attention task, eye-tracking verification, causal brain intervention or actual human–robot social exchange is reported.

public_supplement.read_scope: Entire TableS1 text and visual layout,23 displayed questions covering agency, experience, social understanding and relationships; not a separately validated multidimensional factor model.

study.participants: 22 paid right-handed George Mason undergraduates, seven women; mean age24.36,SD4.73. Normal/corrected vision and no reported neurological/CNS-medication exclusions. Small selected sample; six images and many trials do not create independent hundreds of participants.
study.ethics: Institutional office of integrity and assurance approval and informed consent stated; no clinical intervention or participant diagnosis inferred.
study.stimuli: Six20%-increment morphs between one MekaS2 robot head and one adult male face. Morphing simultaneously changes multiple physical/low-level features; a single identity pair cannot establish universal human/robot differences. The target human image is not a real interacting partner.
study.order: Mind ratings always precede attention testing. Agent order in the attention task and target/response details are counterbalanced/randomized as described; task order itself is fixed. Prior explicit mind judgments, repeated exposure and fatigue could affect subsequent attention.
study.mind_task: Eight-point judgments of internal-state capability. Reported four blocks of12 questions,72 image trials per block,24 questions each twice; the text also says each of six faces appears72 times. The first accounts imply288 total presentations,48 per face; the last implies432. Actual event logs are needed. Supplement TableS1 supplies23 questions, leaving a further item-count discrepancy.
study.attention_task: Outside scanner, static gaze shifts precede letter F/T targets. Targets occur opposite gaze80% versus gazed-at20%; participants respond to letter identity, with a1200ms timeout. Gaze effect=invalid-location RT minus valid-location RT. Positive cueing can reflect reflexive orienting despite counterprediction; negative cueing can reflect useful learning/voluntary orienting. More cue following is not uniformly better task performance.
study.behavior_models: Authors compare linear through fourth-order mixed models using likelihood-ratio comparisons and BIC, then deliberately fit a linear mediation model. A nonlinear mind/appearance relationship is reported, but gaze-related models prefer linear by BIC. Exact baseline/df/chi-square values disagree across prose/tables, so model-comparison claims cannot all be reproduced from printed values.
study.behavior_mediation: Reported total standardized effect.15[−.01,.33],p=.08; direct.44[.14,.73],p<.01; indirect−.28[−.52,−.05],p<.01. Figure8 paths.83 and−.34 give product−.2822, compatible with−.28, and rounded direct+indirect can be compatible with total.15. A nonsignificant total does not invalidate suppression or opposing associations.
study.causal_boundary: Mind ratings correlate.83 with physical humanness. Conditioning on a measured mediator/highly correlated covariate can create unstable or model-dependent signs; significant coefficients do not exclude such issues. Authors explicitly acknowledge multicollinearity and later urge caution. A suppression-pattern fit is not proof of the proposed voluntary/reflexive causal pathways.
study.fmri_pipeline: 3T imaging, FSL preprocessing, six motion covariates, mixed group analysis and whole-brain cluster correction, cluster-formingZ1.96, nominalFWER.05. These are reported analytic settings, not an independent verification that assumptions or correction behavior hold for the dataset.
study.planned_vs_posthoc: All four runs in the planned mind-rating parametric analysis yield no corrected significant cluster. The authors explicitly disclose a post hoc first-two-run analysis motivated by possible habituation, which yields a corrected medial/frontal cluster. Habituation is an explanation, not an independently established reason for the changed significance.
study.gaze_weighted_analysis: All four scanner runs are weighted by each participant’s later, per-face gaze effect. This associates earlier fMRI patterns with later reaction-time summaries. A conjunction with the post hoc mind-rating map is not direct neural activity measured during attention or proof the same neurons perform both computations.
study.localization: The text describes gaze-weightedvmPFC peakZ3.59 at−46,38,−2,982voxels. Table4 assigns that peak to frontal-pole/orbitofrontal/inferior-frontal cluster1, while the listedvmPFC subpeaks appear in cluster5. The printed peak reference needs clarification; Table4 does includevmPFC subpeaks, so do not conclude that no medial-prefrontal activation exists.
study.alternative_interpretations: Authors discuss predictability, eeriness, task demands, anthropomorphism and lateralization/power as alternatives. Brain-region overlap is not a unique marker of mentalizing, motor resonance, empathy or conscious feeling. The findings do not demonstrate brain-structure changes, despite the broad title wording.
study.measurement_scope: The supplement pools agency, feeling and relationship questions; this paper does not separately validate two agency/experience factors. Rating that a face has a mind differs from accurately inferring its beliefs or demonstrating that a robot has mental states.

chi_square_reconstructions.location: Table2 cubic gaze comparison, conditional on a single added polynomial term
Table1 cubic increment, conditional on one added term

mediation_rounding.interpretation: Product and sum can be compatible with rounded coefficients; a nonsignificant total does not invalidate opposite-sign direct/indirect associations.

summary: Add gaze cueing as a measured attention construct and motor resonance as an explicitly secondary theoretical construct. Enrich mind/agency/experience attribution with measurement limits. Preserve planned correction-null versus post hoc significant imaging results, adaptive counterpredictive attention and multicollinearity cautions. Correct verified source identifiers/volume and reversed table labeling; retain unresolved trial, item, statistic and peak-reference disagreements without guessed repairs.

findings.definition: Orienting attention in response to another entity’s gaze direction.
findings.ai_evidence_status: Human attention task using static human–robot face morphs; proposed AI analogue not tested
findings.novelty_rationale: A specific visual-social cueing process absent from existing general attention capture and mind-attribution entries. It does not require joint awareness, belief inference or emotional contagion.

evidence.quote: Gaze-cueing effects were calculated by subtracting reaction

findings.evidence_scope: Participants identify letters after gaze shifts from six face morphs. Targets are counterpredicted by gaze, so direction and utility depend on learning/expectations. Reported total and mediation associations are qualified by small sample, appearance confounds and model/reporting limits; neural causal interpretation remains unresolved.
findings.boundary: Gaze following, reflexive attention, learned counterprediction, mutual joint attention and actual mentalizing differ. A smaller/reversed cue effect can be adaptive in this task. Transformer attention and a model’s textual focus do not establish human visual orienting or machine experience.
findings.ai_proposal: Test a vision-capable agent with matched scenes in which gaze indicates one location but verified task-relevant targets may be elsewhere. Measure whether it uses gaze appropriately, learns reliability and avoids treating a social cue as decisive evidence without task support.

findings.definition: Activation of shared action representations during observation and execution of similar actions.
findings.ai_evidence_status: Secondary neurocognitive construct discussed; motor resonance not measured here and AI analogue untested
findings.novelty_rationale: Shared motor representation differs from learning by observation, copying a statement, emotional contagion or merely inferring another’s beliefs. Earlier narrative references did not supply a sufficiently reviewed definition.

evidence.quote: activated both when an action is executed

findings.evidence_scope: The introduction defines resonance through shared representations in observed/executed action and discusses debated mirror-neuron interpretations. This study’s empirical tasks are ratings and gaze cueing, not a new motor-resonance experiment or proof of a human mirror mechanism.
findings.boundary: Neural overlap, automatic imitation, motor interference, observational learning and empathic feeling are distinct. No shared biological neurons, feelings or identical human mechanism follows from an AI matching actions; do not credit cited primate/human experiments as separately read sources.
findings.ai_proposal: For an embodied or action-capable model, test transfer between recognizing an observed action and executing a matching goal under controlled conditions. Compare perception-only and execution-only baselines; describe observable representation/behavior transfer without claiming a biological mirror system.

findings.definition: Attributing to another entity a capacity for intentional thought, planning and action.
findings.novelty_rationale: Existing construct; add the measurement context and explicit inference limits rather than a duplicate mind-perception label.

evidence.quote: the agents’ capability of having internal states

findings.evidence_scope: Face-morph ratings include planning, choices and acting independently, alongside other mind items. Physical appearance and pooled ratings are associated, but agency is not independently isolated as a factor or experimentally manipulated independently of appearance.
findings.boundary: Perceived capability, physical human likeness, actual agency, moral responsibility and sentience differ. Brain activation during a rating task does not prove a robot has internal states or identify a unique attribution process.

findings.definition: Attributing to another entity the capacity for subjective feelings or sensations, such as pleasure, pain, fear or joy.
findings.novelty_rationale: Existing construct; add the measurement context and explicit inference limits rather than a duplicate mind-perception label.
findings.evidence_scope: The theoretical framework and supplementary questions include happiness, sadness, feelings and pain within a general mind-rating task. This is attribution-related measurement, not separate evidence of machine feeling or a validated experience factor in this sample.
findings.boundary: General pooled mind ratings, perceived feelings, actual subjective experience and empathy differ. The planned imaging analysis was correction-null; post hoc activation cannot be presented as direct sentience evidence.

findings.definition: Attributing human characteristics, intentions, emotions or other mental states to a nonhuman entity.
findings.novelty_rationale: Existing construct; add the measurement context and explicit inference limits rather than a duplicate mind-perception label.
findings.evidence_scope: One robot/human face pair is morphed at six levels to examine mind ratings and subsequent attention. The manipulation changes appearance, and explicit judgments precede gaze testing; observed associations need not uniquely reflect anthropomorphic belief.
findings.boundary: Human likeness, low-level visual properties, belief, familiarity and social attention are not interchangeable. No uniform performance benefit, real relationship improvement, clinical inference or actual model mentality is established.

findings.definition: Inferring another’s beliefs, intentions, desires or emotions to explain or anticipate their behavior.
findings.novelty_rationale: Existing construct; add the measurement context and explicit inference limits rather than a duplicate mind-perception label.

evidence.quote: such as beliefs, intentions, and emotions

findings.evidence_scope: Mentalizing is defined as inferring internal states, but the current scanner task mainly asks whether an entity has capacities; it is not a direct false-belief or accurate belief-inference task.
findings.boundary: Mind-capacity attribution and accurate mental-state inference differ. Brain-region overlap, later reaction times and anthropomorphic appearance do not independently validate mentalizing ability; this boundary does not fill a paper gap.

source_corrections.correction: The exact-title Cullen/Kanai/Bahrami/Rees paper has DOI10.1093/scan/nst109; the truncated DOI returned404. Online2013 and print2014,9(9),1276–1280 are compatible dates, so retain valid date distinctions.
source_corrections.scope: Bibliographic identity only; original not independently fully read.

source_corrections.correction: Crossref identifies volume12,issue5,pages582–593, print2017, with online publication2 September2016. Correct volume2 to12 and distinguish the valid online2016 date from the2017 issue rather than declaring the whole citation nonexistent.

source_corrections.reported: Predicting mind rating data from gaze-cueing data.
source_corrections.correction: The surrounding Methods/Results and Figure7 describe predicting gaze-cueing behavior from mind ratings while accounting for physical humanness. Clarify the reversed caption; do not reverse the regression outcome or fabricate a new analysis.

unresolved_source_discrepancies.finding: Four blocks×72 and24 questions×two repetitions×six faces imply288 presentations, whereas72 appearances per face imply432. TableS1 visibly lists23 questions rather than24. Actual logs/item source are needed; do not silently correct counts.

Reported chi-square values, degrees of freedom, p-values and comparison baselines are not consistently aligned. For example4.51 withdf2 givesp≈.105 rather than.03, while Table2 lists2.51,p=.03. Serial versus linear-baseline comparisons may explain some differences, but exact original output is needed. BIC preference for simpler gaze models is retained without inventing repaired tests.

unresolved_source_discrepancies.location: PDF11–13, gaze-weighted peak description and Table4
unresolved_source_discrepancies.finding: The text labels the−46,38,−2/982-voxel peak asvmPFC; Table4 associates it with a lateral frontal cluster and separately listsvmPFC peaks in cluster5. Clarify the intended peak/cluster reference. Do not infer that allvmPFC activation is absent.

Statistical significance does not itself eliminate multicollinearity/model-instability concerns. Authors acknowledge the.83 correlation and later caution; preserve that caveat instead of presenting suppression as uniquely causal.

methodological_limits: Small selected sample, one face-identity pair, fixed task order and many correlated appearance/mentalizing cues limit generalization.
Counterpredictive attention makes greater gaze following potentially maladaptive; reaction-time differences are not a general social-competence score.
Measured-mediator suppression with highly correlated predictors and intentionally linear modeling does not identify a unique causal cognitive pathway.
Planned correction-null imaging results and disclosed post hoc first-two-run significance must remain separate. No imaging during attention, causal manipulation or unique process-to-region mapping.
Trial/item counts, model-comparison statistics and a peak cross-reference remain unresolved without raw data/code. Source repairs do not validate disputed empirical details.

cross_paper_learning.finding: Questionnaire content and pooled mind attribution matter: the current mixed23-item supplement does not establish independent agency/experience factors, just as correlated adjective factors are not knowledge-free or universally valid dimensions.

A narrative distinction among stances and social-brain processes is not proof of one uniquely activated mechanism. This primary fMRI study supplies data but remains appearance-confounded and includes explicitly post hoc results.

Inspect printed figures and tables before accepting a mechanism narrative. Here the opposite-sign mediation arithmetic can be compatible with rounding, unlike declaring every discrepancy computationally impossible.
Neural overlap, attributed experience and empathic response differ. This source tests human mind ratings/attention, not robot pain or AI feelings.

deferred.term: Joint attention / social facilitation / motor interference
deferred.reason: Relevant cited phenomena, but not sufficiently defined/tested as separate constructs in the current source. Read originals before adding further entries.

deferred.term: Suppression effect / neural conjunction / mirror neurons
deferred.reason: Statistical pattern, analysis operation or cell type rather than an additional behavior entry; keep these in methods and inference boundaries.

deferred.term: vmPFC-driven social competence / intentionality-based gaze avoidance
deferred.reason: Proposed interpretations, not uniquely identified causal mechanisms or actual machine competence.

limitations: Two new human constructs; gaze cueing is measured and motor resonance is secondary theory. No independent credits for unread original experiments, fabricated yearly series, automatic harm/principle edges, clinical diagnosis or brain-to-AI equivalence claim.
